# Authentication

Learn how to authenticate your requests to the MrScraper API using API tokens, including best practices for security and usage.

The MrScraper API uses API token authentication to secure all endpoints. Every API request must include a valid API token in the request headers to access the API.

## Getting Your API token

Click your profile icon in the top-right corner of the dashboard.

Select API Tokens.

Click New Token.

Enter a token name and choose an expiration date.

Note

The token name is required when making requests to the analytics endpoint.

Click Create.

Copy the generated API token and store it in a secure location. You will need this token to authenticate API requests.

Keep It Secret!

Never expose your API token in client-side code (like browsers or apps). Always store it securely in an environment variable or server configuration.

API token Scope

Your API token provides access to:

  * V3 Platform endpoints - All endpoints in the V3 API
  * Sync endpoints - Endpoints on the `sync.scraper.mrscraper.com` host

Click Create , then copy and securely store the generated token. Keep Your Token Secure Your API token grants access to your account and plan resources. Never expose your token in client-side code (like browsers or mobile apps), and store it securely in an environment variable or server configuration. Authenticating Requests Include your API token in the x-api-token HTTP header on every request: x-api-token : <MRSCRAPER_API_TOKEN> Marketplace Endpoints For Marketplace endpoints , authenticate using the standard RFC 6750 Authorization header with a Bearer token: Authorization : Bearer <MRSCRAPER_API_TOKEN> Verify Token To test your authentication and confirm that your token is valid, make a request to the /subscription-accounts endpoint: curl -X GET "https://api.app.mrscraper.com/api/v1/subscription-accounts" \ -H "accept: application/json" \ -H "x-api-token: <MRSCRAPER_API_TOKEN>" Analytics Authentication Analytics endpoints authenticate using the same x-api-token header as all other API endpoints. When querying analytics, you can also pass the apiTokenName query parameter to filter status data for a specific token by the name you assigned when creating it: curl -X GET "https://api.app.mrscraper.com/api/v1/analytic/statuses?domain=example.com&startDate=2026-04-12%2000:00:00&endDate=2026-04-13%2023:59:59&apiTokenName=YOUR_TOKEN_NAME" \ -H "accept: application/json" \ -H "x-api-token: <MRSCRAPER_API_TOKEN>" Note The apiTokenName query parameter filters metrics by the token's name (e.g., production-worker ). pages.text:
MCP Server | MrScraper Documentation Documentation Core Features Dashboard Getting Started Overview Quickstart Web Search Scraper API Token Plan CLI MCP Server Billing Features Workflow Workflow API Access Bulk Scraping Proxy Marketplace Schedule S3 Storage Scraping Tips Cookie Team Guides Common Use Case Optimizing Cost Create and Run a Scraper Programmatically Bulk Scraping With Custom Scraper Integrations Email SQL/Database Webhook Zapier ClawHub x402 n8n Dify Scalekit SDKs MCP Server Official MrScraper MCP server for retrieving web pages, web search, and account usage. Connect AI clients or run the open-source server locally. MrScraper MCP is the official Model Context Protocol server for MrScraper.
It connects AI clients to web page retrieval, web search, and your account
usage. MrScraper MCP server source code on GitHub · Install the @mrscraper/mcp npm package The server exposes seven tools: status Return the raw account status API response without summarizing, redacting body fields, or adding calculated fields. scrapeHtml Retrieve the raw HTML of a page. Browser rendering is optional. scrapeMarkdown Retrieve a page as Markdown. Including HTML also enables browser rendering and returns both outputs as JSON. getScreenshot Capture a base64 screenshot of the full page or top viewport. Browser rendering is always enabled. scrapeBrand Extract a website's colors, typography, logos, and social links as JSON. scrapeJson Extract structured JSON from a page using a natural-language prompt. Append Json Schema: and a JSON schema to shape the output. webSearch Search the web and return ranked results with titles, URLs, descriptions, and sources. Use the hosted Streamable HTTP endpoint for a managed connection, or run the
published MCP package locally through Streamable HTTP or stdio. Package information This page documents @mrscraper/mcp version 0.5.0 . Its seven tools share their descriptions, inputs, and defaults with the MrScraper CLI, SDKs, and integrations. 0.5.0 replaced scraperAPI with scrapeHtml , scrapeMarkdown , and getScreenshot , added scrapeBrand and scrapeJson , renamed the inputs to camel case, and changed the OAuth scopes. See Migration from the previous tool set . Capabilities Page Retrieval Retrieve a known URL as HTML, Markdown, or a screenshot, with optional
browser rendering, real-device routing, proxy controls, selector waiting,
and retry limits. Brand and JSON Extraction Extract a website's colors, typography, logos, and social links, or
structured JSON from a natural-language prompt. Web Search Search the web for ranked results, for a chosen country and up to 100
results at a time. Account Status Read the subscription, token limit, token usage, remaining tokens, and rate
limit. Managed Endpoint Connect to the hosted MCP endpoint through Streamable HTTP with OAuth 2.1
browser sign-in. Structured Tool Results Receive a consistent response envelope in MCP structured content. Interactive Widgets Render search results and an account usage meter in hosts that support MCP
Apps. Requirements A MrScraper account An MCP client with Streamable HTTP support An API key only when the client cannot use
OAuth 2.1 or when running the server locally Quick start with the hosted server Add the hosted endpoint Configure a Streamable HTTP server named mrscraper with no credential: { "mcpServers" : { "mrscraper" : { "type" : "http" , "url" : "https://mcp.mrscraper.com/mcp" } } } Use this exact URL, including the /mcp path. Sign in Connect or reload the MCP server. Your client follows the OAuth 2.1
challenge, opens MrScraper in your browser, and asks you to approve scrape:read for the six scraping and search tools and account:read for status . Reload and verify Reload the client or start a new session, then inspect its MCP tool list.
The connection should expose status , scrapeHtml , scrapeMarkdown , getScreenshot , scrapeBrand , scrapeJson , and webSearch . Copyable AI setup prompt Connect MrScraper MCP to this agent. Detect the current MCP client and use its native Streamable HTTP setup to add a server named mrscraper at exactly https://mcp.mrscraper.com/mcp with no static credential. Complete the OAuth 2.1 browser sign-in; if it does not start automatically, use the client's MCP login or authenticate command. Only if the client does not support OAuth, fall back to a MrScraper API key from https://app.mrscraper.com/api-tokens stored through the client's environment-variable or secret-storage mechanism and sent as Authorization: Bearer <key>. Reload the MCP client when required, then list the tools and confirm that status, scrapeHtml, scrapeMarkdown, getScreenshot, scrapeBrand, scrapeJson, and webSearch are available. Client configuration Add the hosted URL without a static Authorization header, then complete
browser sign-in when the client prompts you. Codex codex mcp add mrscraper \ --url https://mcp.mrscraper.com/mcp Codex uses OAuth by default for Streamable HTTP servers. If browser sign-in does
not start automatically, run codex mcp login mrscraper . Claude Code claude mcp add \ --transport http \ --scope user \ mrscraper https://mcp.mrscraper.com/mcp Open /mcp inside Claude Code and authenticate, or run claude mcp login mrscraper from your shell. To add MrScraper's three skills for page retrieval and web search along with
the server, install the MrScraper plugin for Claude Code instead: claude plugin marketplace add mrscraper-com/mrscraper-claude-plugin claude plugin install mrscraper@mrscraper-claude The plugin is also listed on ClaudePluginHub . Claude and Claude Desktop Open the custom connector form In a general Claude chat, select the + button below the input box, then
choose Connectors → Add connector → Add custom connector . Add MrScraper Enter MrScraper as the name and https://mcp.mrscraper.com/mcp as the MCP server URL, then select Continue . Sign in Complete the MrScraper OAuth browser flow when Claude prompts you. Cursor Open Cursor Settings → Tools & MCP → Add Custom MCP , then add: { "mcpServers" : { "mrscraper" : { "type" : "http" , "url" : "https://mcp.mrscraper.com/mcp" } } } Refresh the MCP server list, then authenticate when prompted. VS Code Add the server to your user settings: { "mcp" : { "servers" : { "mrscraper" : { "type" : "http" , "url" : "https://mcp.mrscraper.com/mcp" } } } } For a workspace configuration, place the server object under servers in .vscode/mcp.json . Start the server and VS Code opens a browser for OAuth. Windsurf Add the following entry to the Windsurf MCP configuration: { "mcpServers" : { "mrscraper" : { "serverUrl" : "https://mcp.mrscraper.com/mcp" } } } Refresh the MCP server list, then complete OAuth when prompted. Other MCP clients Use these connection values: Setting Value Name mrscraper Transport Streamable HTTP URL https://mcp.mrscraper.com/mcp Authentication OAuth 2.1; do not configure a static header API key fallback If a client cannot complete OAuth, create an API key ,
store it through the client's secret mechanism, and send it as a bearer token: { "mcpServers" : { "mrscraper" : { "type" : "http" , "url" : "https://mcp.mrscraper.com/mcp" , "headers" : { "Authorization" : "Bearer YOUR_MRSCRAPER_API_KEY" } } } } For Codex, pass the environment-variable name instead of embedding the key: export MRSCRAPER_API_KEY = "YOUR_MRSCRAPER_API_KEY" codex mcp add mrscraper \ --url https://mcp.mrscraper.com/mcp \ --bearer-token-env-var MRSCRAPER_API_KEY Authentication Connection Credential source Hosted Streamable HTTP OAuth 2.1 browser sign-in, or an API key fallback Self-hosted Streamable HTTP OAuth 2.1 access token, or Authorization: Bearer <MrScraper API key> Local stdio MRSCRAPER_API_KEY , then MRSCRAPER_API_TOKEN The hosted server publishes OAuth 2.1 protected-resource metadata and challenges
unauthenticated clients to start browser sign-in. Access tokens are issued for
the exact https://mcp.mrscraper.com/mcp resource. A tool called without its
required scope returns 403 insufficient_scope , and your client can offer to
grant the missing permission. Scope Tools scrape:read scrapeHtml , scrapeMarkdown , getScreenshot , scrapeBrand , scrapeJson , and webSearch account:read status These are the only application scopes the server advertises; the
authorization server also offers offline_access for refresh tokens. Clients
take the scopes from the server's metadata, so don't pin scopes in client
configurations. OAuth connections that already hold scrape:read keep working without
reconnecting; scrape:write is no longer needed by any tool. Connections
without scrape:read must reconnect and approve it to run the scraping and
search tools; status still uses account:read . API keys remain supported for clients without OAuth and carry full account
authority, so no scope is enforced against them. Authentication stays at the
transport layer; tools never accept credentials as arguments. Run the MCP server locally Node.js 20 or newer is required. Published package over stdio { "mcpServers" : { "mrscraper" : { "command" : "npx" , "args" : [ "-y" , "@mrscraper/mcp@latest" ], "env" : { "MRSCRAPER_API_KEY" : "YOUR_MRSCRAPER_API_KEY" } } } } Source checkout over Streamable HTTP Clone and build git clone https://github.com/mrscraper-com/mrscraper-mcp.git cd mrscraper-mcp npm ci npm run build Start HTTP transport TRANSPORT = http npm start The default endpoint is http://127.0.0.1:8000/mcp . Connect the client { "mcpServers" : { "mrscraper" : { "type" : "http" , "url" : "http://127.0.0.1:8000/mcp" , "headers" : { "Authorization" : "Bearer YOUR_MRSCRAPER_API_KEY" } } } } Docker docker build -f docker/Dockerfile -t mrscraper-mcp . docker run --rm -p 8000:8000 mrscraper-mcp The image binds to 0.0.0.0 . Apply network controls appropriate for the
deployment and keep bearer verification enabled. Environment variables Variable Default Purpose TRANSPORT stdio Selects stdio or http . HOST 127.0.0.1 HTTP bind address; the Docker image uses 0.0.0.0 . PORT 8000 HTTP listen port. MRSCRAPER_API_KEY — Primary stdio credential. MRSCRAPER_API_TOKEN — Alternative stdio credential, also used by the Python SDK. MRSCRAPER_HTTP_AUTH 1 Enables HTTP bearer verification. MRSCRAPER_OAUTH 1 Accepts OAuth 2.1 access tokens alongside API keys. MRSCRAPER_MCP_PUBLIC_URL https://mcp.mrscraper.com Public origin; <origin>/mcp is the required token audience. MRSCRAPER_OAUTH_ISSUER https://api.app.mrscraper.com Authorization server issuer. MRSCRAPER_OAUTH_JWKS_URL <issuer>/.well-known/jwks.json Key set used to verify access tokens. MRSCRAPER_ALLOWED_ORIGINS — Comma-separated browser origins allowed to call the HTTP server. MRSCRAPER_API_BASE_URL MrScraper platform API Platform endpoint override used by status . MRSCRAPER_FETCH_BASE_URL MrScraper Scraper API Endpoint override used by the six scraping and search tools. MRSCRAPER_LOG_HTTP_PAYLOAD off Enables trusted-environment request-body diagnostics. MRSCRAPER_LOG_HTTP_PAYLOAD_MAX 8192 Maximum diagnostic payload length. Security behavior HTTP authentication is enabled by default. Credential-bearing response headers are filtered from tool output. Credential metadata in scraping and search responses is redacted, and
network errors redact signed query credentials. status preserves every field of the account status response body,
including account identity and billing identifiers. Only credential-bearing
response headers are removed. Browser-origin requests are accepted from trusted local origins, from claude.ai and chatgpt.com , and from exact
values configured through MRSCRAPER_ALLOWED_ORIGINS . Tool calls receive the caller's authenticated OAuth token or API key through
the MCP transport rather than through tool arguments. Choosing the right tool Starting point Desired outcome Tool A known URL Raw HTML scrapeHtml A known URL Markdown, or Markdown and HTML together scrapeMarkdown A known URL A screenshot of the full page or top viewport getScreenshot A website Colors, typography, logos, and social links scrapeBrand A known URL Data extracted as JSON with a natural-language prompt scrapeJson A topic or keyword Search result discovery webSearch An account Plan, token usage, and remaining tokens status A discovery workflow commonly uses webSearch first, followed by scrapeMarkdown or scrapeHtml for the pages that will inform the answer.
Agents produce summaries, tables, and structured output from the retrieved
content, or call scrapeJson to have MrScraper extract the data. Migration from the previous tool set Version 0.5.0 replaces the tools and inputs of version 0.4: Previous Replacement scraperAPI scrapeHtml for raw HTML, scrapeMarkdown for Markdown (with html: true , Markdown and HTML), or getScreenshot for a screenshot. Brand and JSON extraction are the separate scrapeBrand and scrapeJson tools. scraperAPI inputs geo_code , proxy_country , browser_rendering , wait_for_selector , block_resources , max_retries , and home_page geoCode , proxyCountry , browserRendering , waitForSelector , blockResources , maxRetries , and warmStart . scraperAPI inputs use_proxy , bypass_proxy , cookie_jar , headers , token_cap , stream , and discard_token_secret Removed. webSearch inputs url , region , num_results , and timeout query , country , and numResults . query is search text; a search results URL is no longer read for its q parameter. The HTTP deadline is fixed at 120 seconds. status summary fields, such as token_remaining and usage_percent The raw account status body, with account details at data.data . OAuth scopes scrape:read and scrape:write scrape:read for all six scraping and search tools; scrape:write is no longer needed. status still uses account:read . Browser rendering no longer switches on automatically. It is off unless browserRendering is true; getScreenshot always renders, and scrapeMarkdown renders when html is true. The page timeout defaults to 300
seconds (was 120), and omitting maxRetries means no retry limit (was 3).
ChatGPT and Codex sign-ins, which got a reduced scraperAPI in 0.4, now
receive the same seven tools and inputs as every other client. Start a new client session or reconnect so the client refreshes its tool list.
OAuth connections that already hold scrape:read keep working; others must
reconnect and approve it. API keys keep working without scope approval. Versions before 0.2.0 exposed fetch , scrape , serp , rerun , results ,
and result . Manage AI scrapers, reruns, and stored results in the MrScraper dashboard . Common response envelope Every tool returns the same envelope in MCP structuredContent and as
formatted JSON in a text content block: { "content" : [ { "type" : "text" , "text" : "[Formatted JSON matching structuredContent]" } ], "structuredContent" : { "status_code" : 200 , "data" : "<html><body>Example page content...</body></html>" , "headers" : { "content-type" : "text/html; charset=utf-8" } } } Field Type Description status_code number or null HTTP status returned by the MrScraper service, or null when the request ends before an HTTP response arrives. data JSON value, string, or null The API response body, as parsed JSON or text. Its field names are not converted. headers object Response headers with credential-bearing headers filtered out. error string, when present Request failure summary. status preserves the complete account status body without adding summary
fields. Error handling HTTP and network failures set isError: true on the MCP tool result and
include error in the envelope. Network failures use status_code: null .
Invalid inputs, including inputs a tool does not define, are rejected before
any upstream call. Authentication and missing OAuth scopes are enforced by the
HTTP transport before a tool runs. Tool reference Tool names, descriptions, inputs, and defaults match the MrScraper CLI, SDKs,
and integrations. Inputs use camel case and are sent to the API under the same
names. Tools authenticate through the MCP connection and do not accept a token
argument. Tool Title OAuth scope readOnlyHint openWorldHint status Account Status account:read true false scrapeHtml Scrape HTML scrape:read false true scrapeMarkdown Scrape Markdown scrape:read false true getScreenshot Get Screenshot scrape:read false true scrapeBrand Scrape Brand scrape:read true true scrapeJson Scrape JSON scrape:read false true webSearch Web Search scrape:read true true Every tool sets destructiveHint: false . scrapeHtml , scrapeMarkdown , getScreenshot , and scrapeJson are not marked read-only because saveResult can save their results to your dashboard. The six scraping and
search tools use tokens from your plan. Examples use https://example.com as the sample target. Replace it for your
use case. Response examples show the envelope from structuredContent , with
selected keys and types observed in live API responses. Values are
placeholders; page content, base64 images, and arrays are abbreviated. Actual
responses may contain additional fields. Shared parameters HTML, Markdown, screenshots, and JSON extraction share url , timeout , geoCode , proxyCountry , super , waitUntil , proxy , maxRetries , and saveResult . Page defaults are 300 seconds, US geolocation and proxy country,
real-device routing off, and dashboard saving off. Omitted retry limits mean no
limit. HTML, Markdown, and screenshots additionally accept blockResources , waitForSelector , and returnCookie . JSON extraction does not accept these
controls. Browser rendering is optional for HTML, Markdown, and JSON;
screenshots always enable it. Markdown with HTML also enables browser
rendering. The six scraping and search tools send GET requests to the Scraper API with
their inputs as query parameters: GET https://api.mrscraper.com Each tool's table lists its complete inputs. status Return the raw account status API response without summarizing, redacting body fields, or adding calculated fields. status takes no service parameters and calls: GET https://api.app.mrscraper.com/api/v1/subscription-accounts The HTTP deadline is fixed at 600 seconds. It is not a service parameter. Example { "name" : "status" , "arguments" : {} } Response The API body contains message and data. Account details remain nested in data, including subscriptionItem and scraperAllowance. The response envelope therefore exposes account details at data.data. Sensitive response headers are removed. { "status_code" : 200 , "data" : { "message" : "Example response" , "data" : { "id" : "ACCOUNT_ID" , "tokenLimit" : 100000 , "tokenUsage" : 2500 , "stripeStatus" : "active" , "user" : { "name" : "Example user" , "email" : "user@example.com" , "isVerified" : true }, "subscriptionItem" : { "name" : "Example plan" , "tokenLimit" : 100000 }, "scraperAllowance" : { "remaining" : 97500 , "plans" : [ { "remaining" : 97500 } ] } } }, "headers" : { "content-type" : "application/json; charset=utf-8" } } scrapeHtml Retrieve the raw HTML of a page. Browser rendering is optional. The request sets html=true , markdown=false , and screenshot=false . Parameters Parameter Type Default Description url string Required Absolute HTTP or HTTPS URL of the page to process. timeout integer 300 Page load timeout in seconds, from 1 to 300. The HTTP request allows 30 additional seconds. geoCode string "us" Two-letter country code to load the page from, sent in lowercase. proxyCountry string "us" Two-letter country code of the proxy server, sent in lowercase. super boolean false Whether to route the request through real devices. waitUntil string: domcontentloaded , load , networkidle0 , networkidle2 "domcontentloaded" Navigation completion event to wait for: domcontentloaded, load, networkidle0, or networkidle2. proxy string Omitted Custom proxy URL used to load the page. maxRetries integer Omitted Maximum number of retries, as a nonnegative integer. Omit this parameter for no limit. saveResult boolean false Whether to save the result to the dashboard Result tab. blockResources boolean false Whether to block images, fonts, and stylesheets while loading the page. waitForSelector string Omitted Wait for the page to contain the specified CSS selector before returning the result. returnCookie boolean false Whether to include browser session cookies in the response. browserRendering boolean false Whether to render the page in a browser before returning the result. warmStart boolean false Whether to enable warm start for more reliable scraping, at the cost of additional latency. Example { "name" : "scrapeHtml" , "arguments" : { "url" : "https://example.com" , "browserRendering" : true , "warmStart" : true , "waitForSelector" : "body" , "timeout" : 120 , "maxRetries" : 0 } } Response The default response body is HTML text. Additional controls can cause the API to return JSON; the returned structure is preserved. { "status_code" : 200 , "data" : "<html><body>Example page content...</body></html>" , "headers" : { "content-type" : "text/html; charset=utf-8" } } scrapeMarkdown Retrieve a page as Markdown. Including HTML also enables browser rendering and returns both outputs as JSON. The request sets markdown=true and screenshot=false . Setting html to true also sets browserRendering=true . Parameters Parameter Type Default Description url string Required Absolute HTTP or HTTPS URL of the page to process. timeout integer 300 Page load timeout in seconds, from 1 to 300. The HTTP request allows 30 additional seconds. geoCode string "us" Two-letter country code to load the page from, sent in lowercase. proxyCountry string "us" Two-letter country code of the proxy server, sent in lowercase. super boolean false Whether to route the request through real devices. waitUntil string: domcontentloaded , load , networkidle0 , networkidle2 "domcontentloaded" Navigation completion event to wait for: domcontentloaded, load, networkidle0, or networkidle2. proxy string Omitted Custom proxy URL used to load the page. maxRetries integer Omitted Maximum number of retries, as a nonnegative integer. Omit this parameter for no limit. saveResult boolean false Whether to save the result to the dashboard Result tab. blockResources boolean false Whether to block images, fonts, and stylesheets while loading the page. waitForSelector string Omitted Wait for the page to contain the specified CSS selector before returning the result. returnCookie boolean false Whether to include browser session cookies in the response. browserRendering boolean false Whether to render the page in a browser before returning the result. warmStart boolean false Whether to enable warm start for more reliable scraping, at the cost of additional latency. html boolean false Whether to include the page HTML in the response. Example { "name" : "scrapeMarkdown" , "arguments" : { "url" : "https://example.com" , "html" : true , "warmStart" : true } } Response The default response body is Markdown text. Enabling HTML returns JSON containing both HTML and Markdown. With html enabled { "status_code" : 200 , "data" : { "html" : "<html>...</html>" , "markdown" : "# Example page \n\n ..." }, "headers" : { "content-type" : "application/json" } } Default Markdown text { "status_code" : 200 , "data" : "# Example page \n\n Example Markdown content..." , "headers" : { "content-type" : "text/markdown; charset=utf-8" } } getScreenshot Capture a base64 screenshot of the full page or top viewport. Browser rendering is always enabled. The request always sets browserRendering=true , so this tool has no browserRendering input. Parameters Parameter Type Default Description url string Required Absolute HTTP or HTTPS URL of the page to process. timeout integer 300 Page load timeout in seconds, from 1 to 300. The HTTP request allows 30 additional seconds. geoCode string "us" Two-letter country code to load the page from, sent in lowercase. proxyCountry string "us" Two-letter country code of the proxy server, sent in lowercase. super boolean false Whether to route the request through real devices. waitUntil string: domcontentloaded , load , networkidle0 , networkidle2 "domcontentloaded" Navigation completion event to wait for: domcontentloaded, load, networkidle0, or networkidle2. proxy string Omitted Custom proxy URL used to load the page. maxRetries integer Omitted Maximum number of retries, as a nonnegative integer. Omit this parameter for no limit. saveResult boolean false Whether to save the result to the dashboard Result tab. blockResources boolean false Whether to block images, fonts, and stylesheets while loading the page. waitForSelector string Omitted Wait for the page to contain the specified CSS selector before returning the result. returnCookie boolean false Whether to include browser session cookies in the response. screenshot string: full , top "full" Screenshot area to capture: full for the entire page or top for the top viewport. html boolean true Whether to include the page HTML in the response. markdown boolean false Whether to include the page Markdown in the response. Example { "name" : "getScreenshot" , "arguments" : { "url" : "https://example.com" , "screenshot" : "top" , "html" : false , "markdown" : true } } Response The response body contains a base64 screenshot and requested page outputs. The API can still include HTML when HTML output is disabled. { "status_code" : 200 , "data" : { "html" : "<html>...</html>" , "screenshot" : "BASE64_PNG_DATA" , "markdown" : "# Example page \n\n ..." }, "headers" : { "content-type" : "application/json; charset=utf-8" } } scrapeBrand Extract a website's colors, typography, logos, and social links as JSON. Parameters Parameter Type Default Description url string Required Absolute HTTP or HTTPS URL of the page to process. The HTTP deadline is fixed at 120 seconds. It is not a service parameter. The request uses action=brand-scraping and bundle=none ; page controls are
not accepted. Example { "name" : "scrapeBrand" , "arguments" : { "url" : "https://example.com" } } Response The API body contains message and a data object with job_id, status, url, final_url, brand, and error. Brand details are available at data.data.brand in the response envelope. { "status_code" : 200 , "data" : { "data" : { "job_id" : "JOB_ID" , "status" : "succeeded" , "url" : "https://example.com" , "final_url" : "https://example.com" , "brand" : { "name" : "Example brand" , "colors" : { "background" : "#ffffff" , "text" : "#222222" }, "typography" : { "body" : { "font_family" : "Example font" } } }, "error" : null , "bundle_url" : null }, "message" : "Example response" }, "headers" : { "content-type" : "application/json" } } scrapeJson Extract structured JSON from a page using a natural-language prompt. Append Json Schema: and a JSON schema to shape the output. Parameters Parameter Type Default Description url string Required Absolute HTTP or HTTPS URL of the page to process. timeout integer 300 Page load timeout in seconds, from 1 to 300. The HTTP request allows 30 additional seconds. geoCode string "us" Two-letter country code to load the page from, sent in lowercase. proxyCountry string "us" Two-letter country code of the proxy server, sent in lowercase. super boolean false Whether to route the request through real devices. waitUntil string: domcontentloaded , load , networkidle0 , networkidle2 "domcontentloaded" Navigation completion event to wait for: domcontentloaded, load, networkidle0, or networkidle2. proxy string Omitted Custom proxy URL used to load the page. maxRetries integer Omitted Maximum number of retries, as a nonnegative integer. Omit this parameter for no limit. saveResult boolean false Whether to save the result to the dashboard Result tab. prompt string "Extract all data as complete as possible." Instructions describing the data to extract. Append Json Schema: and a JSON schema to shape the output. browserRendering boolean false Whether to render the page in a browser before returning the result. html boolean false Whether to include the page HTML in the response. screenshot boolean false Whether to include a base64 screenshot in the response. The request uses agent=general and GET. If the encoded URL exceeds 8,000
characters, it switches to POST with url , prompt , and agent in the body;
page controls remain in the query. Example { "name" : "scrapeJson" , "arguments" : { "url" : "https://example.com" , "prompt" : "Extract the first 2 items with title and price. Json Schema: { \" type \" : \" array \" , \" items \" :{ \" type \" : \" object \" , \" properties \" :{ \" title \" :{ \" type \" : \" string \" }, \" price \" :{ \" type \" : \" string \" }}, \" required \" :[ \" title \" , \" price \" ]}}" , "browserRendering" : true } } Response Extraction results are in the API body's data field and follow the requested schema. Response metadata includes thread_id, token_usage, status, error, runtime, and cookies. html, markdown, and screenshot can be empty strings when not requested. { "status_code" : 200 , "data" : { "success" : true , "data" : [ { "title" : "Example item" , "price" : "10.00" } ], "thread_id" : "THREAD_ID" , "token_usage" : 1 , "html" : "" , "markdown" : "" , "screenshot" : "" , "status" : "Results ready" , "error" : "" , "runtime" : 1.23 , "cookies" : [] }, "headers" : { "content-type" : "application/json" } } webSearch Search the web and return ranked results with titles, URLs, descriptions, and sources. Parameters Parameter Type Default Description query string Required Search query text, trimmed before sending, containing 1 to 1000 characters. country string "us" Two-letter country code to search from, sent in lowercase. numResults integer 10 Number of search results to request, as an integer from 10 to 100. Fewer results may be returned. The HTTP deadline is fixed at 120 seconds. It is not a service parameter. The request uses action=websearch . Example { "name" : "webSearch" , "arguments" : { "query" : "site:example.com documentation" , "country" : "id" , "numResults" : 20 } } Response The API body contains success, message, a data array, and tokenUsage. Each result includes rank, title, url, description, and source. { "status_code" : 200 , "data" : { "success" : true , "message" : "Example response" , "data" : [ { "rank" : 1 , "title" : "Example result" , "url" : "https://example.com" , "description" : "Example result description." , "source" : "example.com" } ], "tokenUsage" : 1 }, "headers" : { "content-type" : "application/json; charset=utf-8" } } Troubleshooting Tools are missing or outdated 401 Unauthorized 403 insufficient_scope 403 Forbidden Origin Input validation error Upstream timeout Verify a local HTTP server CLI Install, authenticate, and use the MrScraper CLI to retrieve pages as HTML, Markdown, or screenshots, extract brand details and structured JSON, search the web, and check account status. Token Plan | MrScraper Documentation Documentation Core Features Dashboard Getting Started Overview Quickstart Web Search Scraper API Token Plan CLI MCP Server Billing Features Workflow Workflow API Access Bulk Scraping Proxy Marketplace Schedule S3 Storage Scraping Tips Cookie Team Guides Common Use Case Optimizing Cost Create and Run a Scraper Programmatically Bulk Scraping With Custom Scraper Integrations Email SQL/Database Webhook Zapier ClawHub x402 n8n Dify Scalekit SDKs Token Plan Learn how plan tokens and API tokens work in MrScraper, why token usage varies between runs, and how to create your own API token for authentication. MrScraper uses a token-based system for both usage and authentication. Plan Tokens measure how much you can use MrScraper's features, such as running or rerunning scrapers. API Tokens allow you to securely access the MrScraper API, for example, to rerun an existing scraper programmatically. Why Token Usage Varies Token consumption isn't fixed — a few key factors affect how many tokens any given scraper uses: Website Complexity : Heavy JavaScript, dynamic content, or multiple requests increase runtime and token usage. Page Size and Content Density : Larger pages with long articles or extensive metadata produce more input text for AI models to process. Data Volume : Extracting large datasets (e.g., paginated listings) requires more compute and bandwidth. AI Processing Load : Complex instructions or large expected outputs increase input and output token usage. Keep these in mind as you read the pricing tables below — they explain why two runs on the same plan can consume different amounts of tokens. Understanding Plan Tokens Each MrScraper billing plan includes a specific number of tokens .
Tokens represent the compute resources your scraper consumes — similar to how minutes or data are counted in a phone plan. The number of tokens used depends on the type of scraper you run. AI Scraper Token Usage AI Scrapers consume more tokens due to AI processing and additional factors such as: Usage Type Description Conversion Rate Run Tracking Each AI agent run consumes 5 tokens for trace tracking. Reruns and workflows consume 0 tokens for this component. 0 or 5 tokens per run Runtime Time spent processing your task. 1 token per 30 seconds of runtime Input Tokens Amount of text data (prompts or instructions) sent to the AI model. 1 token per ~1,000 input tokens Output Tokens Amount of text generated by the AI model (responses or extracted results). 1 token per ~200 output tokens Example If your AI scraper runs for 90 seconds , processes 5,000 input tokens , and generates 1,000 output tokens , your total token usage would be: Component Calculation Tokens Runtime 90 ÷ 30 3 Input 5,000 ÷ 1,000 5 Output 1,000 ÷ 200 5 Run Trace Fixed 5 Total 18 Note Each run automatically includes trace tracking for debugging and performance monitoring. Input and output tokens are based on how much text the AI model processes and generates. AI Scrapers tend to consume more tokens due to model processing. Runtime tokens are rounded up using the ceiling rule. For example, if your scraper runs for 40 seconds, it will count as 2 tokens (not 1). Workflow and Scrape HTML Token Usage Workflows and Scrape HTML consume tokens based on two factors: runtime and bandwidth . Usage Type Description Conversion Rate Runtime Time your scraper runs. 1 token per 30 seconds Bandwidth Amount of data downloaded or uploaded. 1 token per 0.25 MB Example If your workflow or Scrape HTML request runs for 40 seconds and uses 1.1 MB of bandwidth: Component Calculation Tokens Runtime 40 ÷ 30 = 1.33 → rounded up 2 Bandwidth 1.1 ÷ 0.25 = 4.4 → rounded up 5 Total 7 Note Runtime tokens are rounded up using the ceiling rule. For example, if your
scraper runs for 40 seconds, it will count as 2 tokens (not 1). Scraper API Token Cap The Scraper API token cap limits how many tokens a single scrape can use in the Scraper API. It is available in Workflow and under Retry in every Scraper API use case. For Workflow and Scrape HTML, tokens are counted with the runtime and bandwidth calculations shown in Workflow and Scrape HTML Token Usage . When Retry is enabled, a failed scrape retries automatically. Two limits control how far retrying goes: Max retries : The maximum number of retry attempts (3 by default). Token cap : The maximum total tokens all attempts can use (Unlimited by default). Retrying stops at the first of these: the scrape succeeds, it reaches Max retries, or the running token total reaches the token cap. Each attempt's token cost is rounded up (ceiling rule) and added to a running total. The token cap takes effect only when Retry is enabled, since its purpose is to limit how many tokens retries can consume. If Retry is off, the scrape runs once and returns a result or an error. Example The scrape succeeds Stops at Max retries Stops at the Token Cap Max retries 3 , token cap 10 . Attempt Runtime + Bandwidth Rounded-up Cost Running Total Result 1 (initial) 2.4 tokens 3 3 Failed, retrying 2 (retry 1) 1.6 tokens 2 5 Succeeded The scrape succeeds on the second attempt, using 5 tokens. Because it succeeded, the Scraper API returns the result and stops even though max retries and tokens still remain (5 of 10 tokens left, and 2 retries unused). Max retries 2 , token cap 20 . Attempt Runtime + Bandwidth Rounded-up Cost Running Total Result 1 (initial) 3.6 tokens 4 4 Failed, retrying 2 (retry 1) 3.8 tokens 4 8 Failed, retrying 3 (retry 2) 3.4 tokens 4 12 Failed, max retries reached The scrape uses both retries without succeeding, so it stops even though 8 tokens still remain under the 20-token cap. Max retries 3 , token cap 12 , about 4 tokens per run. Attempt Runtime + Bandwidth Rounded-up Cost Running Total Result 1 (initial) 3.5 tokens 4 4 Failed, retrying 2 (retry 1) 3.9 tokens 4 8 Failed, retrying 3 (retry 2) 3.7 tokens 4 12 Failed, cap reached The running total reaches the 12-token cap on the second retry, so the scrape stops before using all 3 retries. First attempt exceeds the cap If the first attempt costs more than the cap (for example, a cap of 10 but a first scrape that needs 15 tokens), the scrape still runs once but doesn't retry. It returns either a result or an error. Set the token cap high enough to allow for retries, especially on pages with variable load times or bandwidth. If a scrape hits the cap before completing, try increasing the cap. Marketplace Scraper Token Usage Marketplace Scrapers use a custom token cost based on factors such as the target domain, workflow complexity, proxy usage, infrastructure requirements, and scraper configuration. Each scraper may use either a fixed token cost or a custom usage calculation depending on how the scraper is designed. For the complete list of Marketplace Scraper token costs, see the Marketplace catalog.
